title: Grounding a support assistant in fast-changing knowledge
prompt: Your support assistant must answer questions using company-specific knowledge (policies, product details, pricing) that changes weekly. Replies must reflect the latest facts and be grounded in real sources. Which approach fits best?
constraint: Knowledge changes frequently; answers must stay current and grounded in authoritative sources.

options.why: The constraint demands current, grounded answers over weekly-changing knowledge. RAG reads the up-to-date KB at request time, so a doc edit is reflected immediately, and retrieved passages give citations for grounding. No retraining cycle stands between a fact changing and the assistant using it — best fit.

Fine-tuning bakes facts into weights, so every weekly change forces a retrain-and-redeploy cycle — the knowledge is stale between runs and the constraint requires it stay current. It also teaches style/format better than volatile facts, and offers no citations for grounding.

A larger base model improves reasoning and fluency but still has no access to private, weekly-changing company knowledge — its training cutoff predates the latest facts. More parameters cannot make answers current or grounded, so it misses the core constraint.

Defensible: RAG still supplies the current, grounded facts the constraint requires, so correctness is preserved. The fine-tuning here is only for stable style/format, not volatile knowledge — but it adds a training pipeline and cost that pure RAG avoids, making it heavier than needed to satisfy the constraint alone.
